titulo: Strategies for understanding and being understood: False friends

aula.titulo: Strategies for understanding and being understood
aula.objetivo: Understand more than you know (similar words, word families, false friends), work around missing words and ask for help without stalling the conversation.

itens.pt: not to know; to ignore (depending on context)
itens.en: not to know; to ignore (depending on context)

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «rester» = to stay: «Je reste à Paris.» (not «to rest») STEP 2: «demander» = to ask (not “to demand”): «Il demande un café.» «Elle demande l'heure.» STEP 3: «attendre» = to wait (not “to attend”): «J'attends le bus.» STEP 4: «exprès» = on purpose (not “express”): «Il l'a fait exprès.» STEP 5: «sale» = dirty (not “sale”): «Mes mains sont sales.» STEP 6: «ignorer» can mean not to know, and can also mean to ignore, depending on context: «J'ignore la réponse.» STEP 7: «magasin» = shop (not «magazine»): «Il y a un magasin près d'ici.» STEP 8: «blesser» = to hurt, to wound (not “to bless”): «Il s'est blessé à la jambe.» STEP 9: «tirer» = to pull (not “to tire”): «Tirez la porte.»
blocos.comparacao: French «attendre» usually means to wait (for), not to attend an event: «assister à» means to attend. «Ignorer» can mean not to know, as in «j’ignore la réponse», or to ignore someone, depending on context.

erros.errado: J'attends le client. (in place of «I serve»)
erros.certo: Je reçois le client. / Je sers le client.

erros.errado: Je demande si tu as faim. (intended meaning: “I demand that you eat”)
erros.motivo: «Demander» commonly means to ask or ask for. For an emphatic demand, «exiger» is often appropriate; context matters.

blocos.enunciado: Say aloud six sentences, one with each false friend: rester, demander, attendre, exprès, sale, ignorer.
Give one example of each shortcut: cognate, word family, prefix.
